target.title: fix: normalize unsupported Anthropic inline images
target.body:
Closes #102323

## Summary

- normalize unsupported Anthropic inline image MIME types at the payload boundary instead of forwarding `image/heic` / `image/tiff` verbatim
- reuse the same normalization path for the packaged Anthropic provider and the custom Anthropic transport
- add regressions for user-image and tool-result image payloads so HEIC/TIFF inputs emit `image/jpeg` before request send

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/media/image-ops.ts src/media/anthropic-inline-images.ts src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`
- `pnpm build`
- `node --import tsx /private/tmp/openclaw-102323-proof.ts`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Anthropic user-image and tool-result payloads no longer send unsupported `image/heic` / `image/tiff` media types verbatim; they normalize to `image/jpeg` before the request leaves OpenClaw.
Real environment tested: ran the real `streamAnthropic()` packaged provider and the real `createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn()` custom transport from this branch against a local 127.0.0.1 loopback Anthropic-compatible capture server that recorded the outbound `/v1/messages` payload and returned a real SSE response shape.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx /private/tmp/openclaw-102323-proof.ts`
Evidence after fix: `/private/tmp/openclaw-102323-proof.json` captured `packaged-user-heic`, `packaged-tool-tiff`, and `transport-user-heic` with `mediaType: "image/jpeg"`, and all three runs returned `stopReason: "stop"` with empty `errorMessage`.
Observed result after fix: the packaged Anthropic provider now sends both HEIC user images and TIFF tool-result images as `image/jpeg`, and the custom Anthropic transport sends HEIC user images as `image/jpeg`; all three requests completed successfully through the real OpenClaw payload builders.
What was not tested: did not hit live `api.anthropic.com`; the proof swaps only the remote endpoint for a loopback capture server, and it does not exercise the wider upstream session/image ingestion paths beyond these Anthropic request builders.
